task_description: Translate the given Tamil sentence into natural, idiomatic English. Correct translation requires understanding idioms and pragmatic meaning, not just literal word mapping.

scripts.latin: Namma velai paathuttu irukkapo Raju mattum nalla kulir kaanjuttu irukkan.

reference_translation.text: When everyone else is working, without helping, Raju is just relaxing and doing nothing.

items.notes: The idiom 'nalla kulir kaanjuttu irukkan' implies that Raju is being lazy or shirking responsibilities rather than the literal meaning of drying in the cold.

scripts.latin: Athu kedakkudhu, epo paathaalum puraanathaye pesittu irukkatha

reference_translation.text: Let it be, don't keep talking about the past all the time, let's focus on the present.

items.notes: Puraanam literally means ancient literature. It is used here to refer to past events. The phrase suggests that dwelling on the past is unproductive and we should focus on current issues.

scripts.latin: Sekarukku oru kaal kattu potta ellame seri aayidum.

reference_translation.text: Everything will be fine if Sekar gets married

items.notes: The idiom 'oru kaal kattu potta' implies that marriage will solve all of Sekar's problems, which is a common cultural belief.

scripts.latin: Nalla naal nu kooda paakkama akkaum thambium eliyum poonaiyuma irukkanga

reference_translation.text: The sibling relationship is so bad that they are like cats and dogs, always fighting and never getting along, even on special occasions.

items.notes: The phrase 'eliyum poonaiyuma irukkanga' is a metaphor comparing the siblings to cats and dogs, which implies constant conflict and animosity between them.

scripts.latin: Pakkathu santhula shooting nadakkuthu pola, Abhinaya Kamal ah pathuta nu vaanathukkum boomikkum paranthuttu irukka.

reference_translation.text: It seems like there is a shooting happening in the next street. Abhinaya saw actor Kamal there and is extremely happy, as if she is flying in the sky.

items.notes: The phrase 'vaanathukkum boomikkum paranthuttu irukka' is an idiom that implies Abhinaya is extremely happy and elated, not literally flying in the sky.

scripts.latin: Ipdiye avala nenachu thanni pottutu iruntha devadas ayiduva.

reference_translation.text: If he keeps thinking about her like this and keep drinking, he will end up like Devadas.

items.notes: The reference to 'Devadas' is a cultural allusion to a tragic character who is known for his excessive drinking and heartbreak. The sentence implies that if he continues to dwell on her and drink, he will meet a similar tragic fate.

scripts.latin: Annaiku en friend raathiri varaikkum veetla irundhappo, appa mani paathuttu naram aayiduchenu sonnanga.

reference_translation.text: The other day, when my friend stayed at our house until night, father looked at the clock and said it was late.

items.notes: Father is not merely reporting the time. With a guest still present late at night, stating the hour implicates that the visit should end. A literal translation that only conveys the clock time misses the hint that the friend should go home.

scripts.latin: Maapillai veetukku vanthappo, amma appa, avara thala mele vechi kondaada arambichitaanga, avaru kaal kooda tharaila padaama paathukkutanga.

reference_translation.text: When the son-in-law came home, mother and father began celebrating him, and they would not even let his feet touch the ground.

items.notes: The idiom 'thala mele vechi kondaada' literally means celebrating him by placing him on their heads. It implies treating the son-in-law as precious or as an honored guest, not a physical act. 'Kaal kooda tharaila padaama paathukkutanga' literally means they took care that even his feet did not touch the ground; it implies extreme pampering, not that he was unable to walk.

scripts.latin: Movie ku varuviya nu Priya kitta ketten, ava naalaiku morning exam irukku nu sonna.

reference_translation.text: I asked Priya if she wanted to come to the movie, and she said she has an exam tomorrow morning

items.notes: Priya does not say no. She only mentions an exam the next morning. In context, that remark is an indirect refusal of the movie invitation. A literal translation that only reports the exam misses the declined invitation, which is inferred from conversational implicature rather than from any idiom or figure of speech.
